alignments.note: Possessive lamed recast as the possessive determiner Their; the preposition keeps nothing (rule 40).

Suffix realized as Their; the ASV's supplied subject They of the second verbless clause resumes the same referent, and the suffix is the only morpheme in the verse denoting it, so both belong to its one discontinuous unit (rule 25). Competing reading: They added under rule 20's closing sentence.

כְּ before the construct דְּמוּת rendered by the single like (rule 30 fusion, headed on the construct noun); the construction-supplied copula joins the fused predicate (rule 49). Competing reading: דְּמוּת unrepresented beside a bare כְּ → is like.
Construct noun takes a supplied the (rule 29).
Prepositional predicate takes the supplied copula (rule 49); the italic subject They placed on the suffix above.
Supplied the belongs to the noun of the expression, not to the adjective (rule 15); discontinuous around deaf.
Relative supplied over an asyndetic finite clause juxtaposed to a written antecedent; no morpheme licenses it (rules 46, 55).

review_notes: Italic They are: They read as a resumption of the suffix's referent (rule 25); are placed on כְּמוֹ under rule 49.
